# package linkage

`import "github.com/lestrrat-3d/decad/linkage"`

<a name="pkg-overview"></a>
## Overview

Package linkage holds the linkage model of agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md —
[Linkage](<#Linkage>), [Link](<#Link>), the sealed [Joint](<#Joint>) set, [Drive](<#Drive>), [LinkageLoop](<#LinkageLoop>) and [Schedule](<#Schedule>) — and
the engines that pose a linkage and verify a drive or a box of joint
values over the motion engine. B is the body reference type: the decad
package instantiates every type here with its own \*Body handle, so callers
normally name them through decad.

<a name="Drive"></a>
### type Drive

<pre>type Drive[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>] []<a href="#JointSweep">JointSweep</a>[B]</pre>

Drive is a one-parameter motion of a linkage, parameterised by the
Dimensionless fraction s ∈ \[0, 1\]: each listed joint passes through its
waypoints From, Via…, To in order, linearly between consecutive ones, and
an unlisted joint holds 0 (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §2.3). A drive
whose sweeps carry n − 1 Via values each has n segments, and segment j
covers s ∈ \[j/n, (j+1)/n\], an equal share each; with no Via the drive is
one segment and each joint runs from From to To as s runs from 0 to 1.

<a name="WithJointLimits"></a>
#### func WithJointLimits

<pre>func WithJointLimits(minimum, maximum units.Value) <a href="#JointOption">JointOption</a></pre>

WithJointLimits declares the joint's working range \[minimum, maximum\], in
the joint's Kind: an Angle for a revolute, a Length for a prismatic. A
wrong Kind is decaderr.ErrUnitKind, a non-finite bound decaderr.ErrNotFinite, and
minimum \>= maximum decaderr.ErrDegenerate. Limits that exclude 0 are legal: the zero
pose then lies outside the working range, and only a drive that visits it is
refused.

Prismatic attaches a new child link of p, holding bodies, on a prismatic
joint sliding along dir (a world direction at the zero pose; only its
direction is used). It refuses, in this order: a nil p or a [Link](<#Link>) no linkage
built (decaderr.ErrDegenerate); an empty bodies, a nil body, or a body listed twice
or already listed in a link of this linkage (decaderr.ErrDegenerate); a non-finite
dir component (decaderr.ErrNotFinite); a dir r3.Vec.Normalize reports no direction
for (decaderr.ErrDegenerate); then the options' own refusals (WithJointLimits).

<a name="Linkage"></a>
### type Linkage

<pre>type Linkage[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Linkage is a tree of links joined by joints, rooted at the ground link. A
link is created only through its parent, so the tree has no cycles. Every
body of the Document that belongs to no link is static.

The zero pose is the document as it stands: every joint value is 0 when the
linkage is built, and a joint's Center, Axis and Dir are world coordinates
at that pose. Building a linkage is not safe for concurrent use; a built
linkage is only read, by PoseAt and VerifyLinkage.

<a name="NewLinkage"></a>
#### func NewLinkage

<pre>func NewLinkage[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>]() *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>[B]</pre>

NewLinkage returns a linkage holding the ground link alone.

<a name="Linkage.Close"></a>
#### func (\*Linkage\[B\]) Close

<pre>func (l *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>[B]) Close(a, b *<a href="#Link">Link</a>[B], center, axis r3.Vec) (*<a href="#LinkageLoop">LinkageLoop</a>[B], <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Close joins a and b, two distinct links of l that already have parents,
with a revolute pin at center about axis (world coordinates at the zero
pose), so the tree gains one loop (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §15.1).
Which joint drives the loop is stated per [Drive](<#Drive>).

It refuses, in this order: a nil linkage, a nil or parentless a or b,
a == b, or a link of another linkage (decaderr.ErrDegenerate); a non-finite center or
axis component (decaderr.ErrNotFinite); the zero axis (decaderr.ErrDegenerate); a loop
revolute whose axis is not exactly parallel to axis, or a loop prismatic
whose direction is not exactly perpendicular to it (decaderr.ErrUnsupported, naming
the joint); two consecutive loop slides along exactly parallel directions
(decaderr.ErrDegenerate); a loop joint already on another loop (decaderr.ErrUnsupported); and
two loop pins of one link coincident in the
loop's plane (decaderr.ErrDegenerate).

<a name="Linkage.Configuration"></a>
#### func (\*Linkage\[B\]) Configuration

<pre>func (l *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>[B]) Configuration(values []units.Value) (<a href="#JointConfiguration">JointConfiguration</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Configuration builds every link's world pose at the stated joint values,
one per link in Links() order (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §14.1). It
composes exactly as PoseAt composes — PoseAt is Configuration of a drive's
values at s — so a renderer drawing a cell and VerifyJointBox evaluating its
centre read the same transform. Every Bounds entry is zero.

It refuses a nil linkage or a value count other than len(Links())
(decaderr.ErrDegenerate); a value of the wrong Kind for its joint (decaderr.ErrUnitKind); a
non-finite value (decaderr.ErrNotFinite); a value outside its joint's declared
limits (decaderr.ErrDegenerate, naming the link); and a pose r3 cannot represent
(decaderr.ErrNotFinite). A linkage with a loop is decaderr.ErrUnsupported: a dependent
joint's value is not the caller's to state. A looped linkage's
configuration is a drive whose every sweep holds, posed by [Linkage](<#Linkage>).PoseAt
or [Schedule](<#Schedule>).PoseAt (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §16.1).

<a name="Linkage.DeclareJointContact"></a>
#### func (\*Linkage\[B\]) DeclareJointContact

<pre>func (l *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>[B]) DeclareJointContact(a, b B) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

DeclareJointContact names a pair of bodies that meet at a joint by
construction — a pin in its bore, a slider on its rail, an arm resting on
its pivot's cap (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §2.2). VerifyLinkage checks
the pair for proven overlap at every evaluated pose and publishes a gap it
measures, but the pair publishes no undecided or touching finding and
enters no interval certificate and no whole-drive reading (§5.4).

a and b MUST belong to different links, or one to a link and the other to
no link. A nil body, a == b, two bodies of one link, two bodies of no link,
and a pair declared twice in either order are decaderr.ErrDegenerate. Liveness and
document membership are checked by VerifyLinkage.

<a name="Linkage.PoseAt"></a>
#### func (\*Linkage\[B\]) PoseAt

<pre>func (l *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>[B]) PoseAt(d <a href="#Drive">Drive</a>[B], at units.Value) (<a href="#LinkagePose">LinkagePose</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

PoseAt returns every link's joint value and world pose at the fraction at
of drive (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §2.4). In segment j of n, between
waypoints w\_j and w\_{j+1}, a joint's value is w\_j + t·(w\_{j+1} − w\_j) with
t = n·at − j, carried in w\_j's unit — From + at·(To − From) for a drive
with no Via — and 0 in its Kind's base unit for an unlisted joint. A
waypoint's fraction j/n takes segment j, and 1 the last segment. A link's pose is its own joint's motion, then its
parent's pose: J\_k(q\_k).Then(Pose\_parent), with J\_k the rotation a Revolute
and the translation a Prismatic of the same axis or direction build, and
the ground's pose the identity; it composes onto each body's own placement
as Transform composes. It is the one place a linkage pose is built, so a
renderer above and VerifyLinkage below evaluate the same transform.

It refuses a nil linkage, a sweep naming no link, the ground, a link of
another linkage or a link twice, and two sweeps carrying different numbers
of Via values (decaderr.ErrDegenerate); a sweep From, To or Via value of the wrong
Kind for its joint (decaderr.ErrUnitKind) or non-finite (decaderr.ErrNotFinite); an at that is
not a finite Dimensionless value (decaderr.ErrUnitKind, decaderr.ErrNotFinite); a waypoint,
or an unlisted joint's 0, outside the joint's declared limits
(decaderr.ErrDegenerate, naming the link); and a pose r3 cannot represent
(decaderr.ErrNotFinite). An at outside \[0, 1\] is legal: PoseAt takes no range, the
first segment's line extends below 0 and the last's above 1, and a drive
whose every sweep holds is legal here.

A drive that moves a loop (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §15) is answered by
a one-shot [Schedule](<#Schedule>) under context.Background(), with [Schedule](<#Schedule>).PoseAt's
refusals: its loop rows, an at outside \[0, 1\], and an at the loop cannot be
enclosed at (decaderr.ErrUnsupported). A renderer that wants one pose per frame
calls [Schedule](<#Schedule>) once instead.

<a name="Linkage.Schedule"></a>
#### func (\*Linkage\[B\]) Schedule

<pre>func (l *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>[B]) Schedule(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, d <a href="#Drive">Drive</a>[B]) (*<a href="#Schedule">Schedule</a>[B], <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[Schedule](<#Schedule>) validates d as PoseAt does and prepares it for repeated PoseAt
calls. For a drive that moves a loop it builds the loop's scene, asks its
zero pose, and asks the drive as one cell, each refused cell replaced by its
two halves down to 1/1024 of the drive. A nil context is decaderr.ErrDegenerate; a
loop the zero pose cannot be enclosed for is decaderr.ErrUnsupported wrapping
sketch's error; a canceled context returns ctx.Err().

<a name="LinkageLoop"></a>
### type LinkageLoop

<pre>type LinkageLoop[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

LinkageLoop is one closure joint of a linkage and the links it ties together
(agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §15.1): a revolute pin joining two links that
both already have parents, so the tree gains one loop. A drive lists at most
one joint of a loop, the driver; every other joint of the loop is dependent,
and its value at a parameter is whatever closes the loop there.

<a name="LinkageLoop.Bars"></a>
#### func (\*LinkageLoop\[B\]) Bars

<pre>func (lp *<a href="#LinkageLoop">LinkageLoop</a>[B]) Bars() []<a href="#LoopBar">LoopBar</a>[B]</pre>

Bars returns the length the loop's private scene holds each link's two loop
pins apart at: Common's bar first, then Links() order. A slide has no bar,
and neither has a link one of whose loop pins is a slide's rail: Common
beside a slide, or a revolute link whose next link slides.

<a name="LinkageLoop.Closure"></a>
#### func (\*LinkageLoop\[B\]) Closure

<pre>func (lp *<a href="#LinkageLoop">LinkageLoop</a>[B]) Closure() <a href="#RevoluteJoint">RevoluteJoint</a></pre>

Closure returns the closing pin as Close stated it, with nil Limits.

<a name="LinkageLoop.Common"></a>
#### func (\*LinkageLoop\[B\]) Common

<pre>func (lp *<a href="#LinkageLoop">LinkageLoop</a>[B]) Common() *<a href="#Link">Link</a>[B]</pre>

Common returns the two closed links' lowest common ancestor: the ground for
a four-bar.

<a name="LinkageLoop.Links"></a>
#### func (\*LinkageLoop\[B\]) Links

<pre>func (lp *<a href="#LinkageLoop">LinkageLoop</a>[B]) Links() []*<a href="#Link">Link</a>[B]</pre>

Links returns every link on the loop but Common, in [Linkage](<#Linkage>).Links() order.

<a name="LinkagePose"></a>
### type LinkagePose

<pre>type LinkagePose struct {
    At  units.Value // the Dimensionless fraction s
    // Values is each link&#39;s joint value at s, in Linkage.Links() order: the
    // stated value, or for a loop&#39;s dependent joint the float midpoint of its
    // certified enclosure (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §15.4).
    Values []units.Value
    // Bounds is each value&#39;s proven half-width, in its Kind: Values[k] ±
    // Bounds[k] holds the exact joint value. It is zero for every joint whose
    // value the drive states.
    Bounds []units.Value
    Poses  []r3.Transform // each link&#39;s world pose at s, in the same order
}</pre>

LinkagePose is every link's pose at one parameter value.

### type LinkagePoseResult

<pre>type LinkagePoseResult[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>] struct {

    Diagnostics   []vocab.<a href="report.md#DiagnosticOf">DiagnosticOf</a>[B, vocab.<a href="report.md#JointCell">JointCell</a>]
}</pre>

LinkagePoseResult records one evaluated pose and its pair findings.

<pre>type LinkageReport[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>] struct {

LinkageReport is VerifyLinkage's drive report (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §4).

<a name="Verify"></a>
#### func Verify

<pre>func Verify[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>](ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, h <a href="#Hooks">Hooks</a>[B], l *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>[B], drive <a href="#Drive">Drive</a>[B],
    options func(motionbound.Domain) (motionoption.Config, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)) (*<a href="#LinkageReport">LinkageReport</a>[B], <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Verify is the engine of Document.VerifyLinkage over a linkage the caller
has already admitted (non-nil, with links, every body live and built):
it resolves the drive, proves the chain bounds and runs the motion engine.
options resolves the caller's options once the drive is known good, so the
drive's refusals precede the options'.

<a name="LinkageReport.Passed"></a>
#### func (\*LinkageReport\[B\]) Passed

<pre>func (r *<a href="#LinkageReport">LinkageReport</a>[B]) Passed() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a></pre>

Passed reports whether the report is Sound. It returns false for nil.

<a name="LoopBar"></a>
### type LoopBar

<pre>type LoopBar[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>] struct {
    Link   *<a href="#Link">Link</a>[B]
    Length vocab.<a href="report.md#Measurement">Measurement</a>
}</pre>

LoopBar is the length a loop's private scene holds one link's two loop
pins apart at (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §15.2): the exact distance, in
the loop's plane, between the pins. The scene states the bar as the
interval \[Length.Value − Length.Bound, Length.Value\], so its claims cover
the exact length; Length is Exact with a zero Bound when the length is a
float.

<a name="PrismaticJoint"></a>
### type PrismaticJoint

<pre>type PrismaticJoint struct {
    Dir    r3.Vec
    Limits *<a href="#JointLimits">JointLimits</a> // nil when none were declared
}</pre>

PrismaticJoint slides its link along Dir by the joint's value, a Length.
Dir is a world direction at the zero pose; only its direction is used.

<a name="RevoluteJoint"></a>
### type RevoluteJoint

<pre>type RevoluteJoint struct {
    Center r3.Vec       // a position, millimetres (core §5.2)
    Axis   r3.Vec       // a direction; only its direction is used
    Limits *<a href="#JointLimits">JointLimits</a> // nil when none were declared
}</pre>

RevoluteJoint rotates its link about the axis through Center along Axis,
right-handed, by the joint's value, an Angle. Center and Axis are world
coordinates at the zero pose.

<a name="Schedule"></a>
### type Schedule

<pre>type Schedule[B <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#comparable">comparable</a>] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Schedule is a drive prepared for repeated PoseAt calls on one linkage
(agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §15.7). For every loop the drive moves it
holds the private scene and the chain of certified enclosures, built as far
as the drive could be certified. Its PoseAt is safe for concurrent use.

<a name="Schedule.Drive"></a>
#### func (\*Schedule\[B\]) Drive

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Schedule">Schedule</a>[B]) Drive() <a href="#Drive">Drive</a>[B]</pre>

[Drive](<#Drive>) returns the drive the schedule was built for.

<a name="Schedule.Linkage"></a>
#### func (\*Schedule\[B\]) Linkage

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Schedule">Schedule</a>[B]) Linkage() *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>[B]</pre>

[Linkage](<#Linkage>) returns the linkage the schedule was built on. [LinkagePose](<#LinkagePose>).Values
and Poses from PoseAt follow its Links() order.

<a name="Schedule.PoseAt"></a>
#### func (\*Schedule\[B\]) PoseAt

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Schedule">Schedule</a>[B]) PoseAt(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, at units.Value) (<a href="#LinkagePose">LinkagePose</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

PoseAt returns every link's joint value, its proven half-width and its
world pose at the fraction at (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §15.4, §15.7).
For a tree linkage it is [Linkage](<#Linkage>).PoseAt with zero Bounds. For a drive that
moves a loop, each dependent joint's value is the float midpoint of its
certified enclosure and Bounds its half-width; an at outside \[0, 1\], or one
whose loop cannot be enclosed, is decaderr.ErrUnsupported wrapping sketch's error.
Two calls at the same at return equal poses bit for bit.
